title: Incidence and Outcomes of Bloodstream Infections in Critically Ill Patients with COVID-19: A Nationwide Multicenter Study in South Korea.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) increases the risk of bloodstream infections (BSI), but associated risk factors remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to evaluate BSI risk factors in patients admitted to the intensive care unit for COVID-19.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This nationwide multicenter study, conducted across 22 university-affiliated hospitals in South Korea, included COVID-19 patients treated with high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy or mechanical ventilation.
analysis.methods: Pathogens were analyzed, risk factors were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, and supplementary Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed to address time-dependent outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Of 573 included patients, 206 (35.9%) developed at least one BSI episode. Staphylococcus species were the most frequent isolates. Gram-negative bacteria became increasingly prevalent over time, while fungal infections were associated with prolonged hospitalization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Multivariable analysis identified chronic neurological disease, higher baseline Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, mechanical ventilation, prone positioning, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) use prior to infection as independent BSI predictors. Notably, although crude in-hospital mortality was significantly higher in the BSI group (41.5% vs. 31.7%, p=0.012), BSI was not an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality in either logistic regression or Cox analyses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: In critically ill patients with COVID-19, high baseline severity, chronic neurological disease, and pre-infection advanced life support (mechanical ventilation and ECMO) were independent predictors of BSI. Rather than acting as an independent cause of death, BSI primarily serves as a clinical marker of extreme illness severity and prolonged invasive interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the risk factors for bloodstream infections (BSI) in critically ill patients with COVID-19 admitted to intensive care units in South Korea. A nationwide multicenter study across 22 hospitals included patients treated with high-flow nasal cannula or mechanical ventilation. Pathogens were analyzed, and risk factors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Of 573 patients, 35.9% developed at least one BSI episode, with Staphylococcus species being the most common. Gram-negative bacteria increased in prevalence over time, and fungal infections were linked to prolonged hospitalization. Independent predictors of BSI included chronic neurological disease, higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores, and prior use of mechanical ventilation or ECMO. Despite higher crude mortality in the BSI group, BSI was not an independent predictor of mortality. The findings highlight BSI as a marker of severe illness and prolonged interventions rather than a direct cause of death. The study provides insights into BSI risk factors in critically ill COVID-19 patients, which could inform clinical management and surveillance strategies.

title: Evolution of the SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 Main Protease Under Fitness Constraints Imposed by Folding Stability and Activity

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the evolutionary constraints on the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) due to its structural and functional requirements, highlighting the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants, focusing on their evolution since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, and examined their structural and functional characteristics across prevalent variants.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted an analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants using ensemble dynamics to assess large-scale motions and substrate-dependent shifts in secondary motions, while also evaluating substrate recognition and interactions across variants.
analysis.main_results: The analysis showed that despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained, with limited amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, which supports its use as an effective antiviral target, and suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics could improve the robustness of therapeutic strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the design of more robust therapeutic strategies against SARS-CoV-2 by considering its evolutionary dynamics, which could enhance long-term antiviral efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on analysis of multiple variants, but the evidence is limited to structural and functional observations, with no direct clinical or epidemiological outcomes reported.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the evolutionary constraints on the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) due to its structural and functional requirements. The researchers analyzed multiple Mpro variants, showing that despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino-acid substitutions in key regions. The findings suggest that Mpro is a suitable antiviral target and that incorporating its evolutionary dynamics may improve the long-term robustness of therapeutic strategies. However, the study's results are based on structural and functional observations without direct clinical or epidemiological outcomes, which limits the strength of the evidence. The study contributes to understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern Mpro evolution and highlights the importance of considering these dynamics in the development of antiviral therapies.

title: Repositioning niclosamide and alectinib to inhibit the hyperphosphorylation of SARS‐CoV‐2's nucleocapsid protein

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of inhibiting SARS-CoV-2's nucleocapsid protein hyperphosphorylation, a process critical for viral replication and genomic RNA unpackaging.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Calu-3 and Vero E6 cells to investigate the effect of GSK-3 inhibition on SARS-CoV-2 replication, with a focus on the virus's nucleocapsid protein and its phosphorylation dynamics.
analysis.methods: The researchers used liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to evaluate the phosphorylation profile of the purified N protein and examined the dose-dependent effect of GSK-3 inhibitors in 293T cells expressing the viral protein.
analysis.main_results: GSK-3 inhibition was found to delay the release of progeny virus from infected cells, and the NR203M and NR204R mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants reduced the efficiency of GSK-3-mediated phosphorylation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as evidence for a novel pharmacological approach that combines niclosamide and alectinib to partially degrade GSK-3 and restore sensitivity to the clinically tested inhibitor enzastaurin.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential new strategy for treating COVID-19 by targeting the phosphorylation of SARS-CoV-2's nucleocapsid protein through the repositioning of existing drugs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to in vitro experiments, and the observed effects on viral release may not fully translate to in vivo settings, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of repositioning niclosamide and alectinib to inhibit the hyperphosphorylation of SARS-CoV-2's nucleocapsid protein, a process mediated by host kinase GSK-3. The research highlights the challenges of conventional kinase inhibition due to the complex and redundant priming mechanism of N hyperphosphorylation. The authors demonstrate that GSK-3 inhibition delays progeny virus release in infected cells and that mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants reduce the efficiency of this process. They propose a novel pharmacological strategy combining niclosamide and alectinib to partially degrade GSK-3 and restore sensitivity to clinically tested inhibitors. While the findings offer a biochemical basis for a new treatment approach, the study's reliance on in vitro models limits its direct applicability to clinical settings, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Long COVID in the pediatric population – clinical evolution, prevalence and management from the early pandemic to the current era: a systematic review

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the clinical evolution, prevalence, and management strategies of Long COVID in pediatric patients from the early pandemic to the current era, as the condition presents a complex clinical picture that has changed over time.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A systematic review of literature published between 2020 and 2026 was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Embase, focusing on observational studies, prospective cohort analyses, and clinical trial data assessing post-acute symptoms in children and adolescents aged 0–18 years.
analysis.methods: The review included studies following PRISMA guidelines, analyzing post-acute symptoms (≥12 weeks post-infection) in pediatric populations, with an emphasis on clinical trajectory, symptom clusters, and therapeutic management strategies.
analysis.main_results: The prevalence of pediatric Long COVID decreased from 10–25% during the pre-Omicron variants to 2–8% in the post-Omicron era, largely influenced by vaccination coverage and hybrid immunity. The most persistent clinical manifestations shifted from systemic fatigue, headache, and dyspnea to persistent fatigue, neurocognitive dysfunction, mood disturbances, and dysautonomia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the evolving nature of Long COVID in children, with a notable shift in symptomatology over time, and emphasized the need for updated therapeutic approaches.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of integrated, multidisciplinary follow-up models and standardized diagnostic criteria to improve long-term clinical management and functional recovery in pediatric patients with Long COVID.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on observational data and the variability in prevalence rates across pandemic phases, but the evidence is strong due to the comprehensive systematic review methodology and inclusion of diverse data sources.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the clinical evolution, prevalence, and management of Long COVID in pediatric populations from the early pandemic to the current era. It highlights the significant decrease in prevalence, influenced by vaccination and hybrid immunity, and the shift in persistent symptoms from systemic manifestations to neurocognitive and autonomic issues. The study underscores the importance of multidisciplinary approaches and standardized diagnostic criteria for effective management. While the review is based on observational data and presents variability in findings, the comprehensive methodology and inclusion of diverse sources support its conclusions. The results have important implications for understanding and addressing the long-term health impacts of SARS-CoV-2 in children.

title: Childhood and adolescent immunisation intentions post-COVID-19 in Lusaka, Zambia

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focused on understanding caregivers’ perceptions of novel vaccinations for children and their intentions to vaccinate children and adolescents ages 12-17 years against SARS-CoV-2 in Lusaka, Zambia. The central question was whether the hesitancy observed with the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine would extend to future novel vaccines for children.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a secondary data analysis of a cross-sectional survey of 277 caregivers of children aged 0-17 years in Lusaka, Zambia, collected between 13 November and 15 December 2023. The study used descriptive statistics to explore demographic characteristics, vaccination history, and caregivers’ perceptions of SARS-CoV-2 and novel vaccines.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that 93.1% of caregivers reported their child had received all recommended routine childhood vaccinations. Caregivers most trusted the Ministry of Health and healthcare professionals as sources of vaccine information. However, overall intention to further vaccinate children against SARS-CoV-2, especially among those already unvaccinated, remained low, with 24.7% of caregivers reporting no intent to vaccinate their children.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study noted that caregivers’ own vaccination status was associated with higher acceptance of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines for their adolescents. However, the evidence does not report on the specific mechanisms or factors influencing vaccine hesitancy, nor does it provide detailed insights into the reasons for reluctance towards future vaccines.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Targeted and transparent communication through trusted sources such as the Ministry of Health and healthcare professionals may be critical for addressing safety concerns and strengthening confidence in novel childhood vaccines. The study highlights the need for improved education and outreach to caregivers about the benefits and risks of vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines caregivers’ perceptions and intentions regarding childhood and adolescent immunization against SARS-CoV-2 in Lusaka, Zambia. It reports that routine childhood vaccine uptake remains high, but acceptance of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines for adolescents is lower. Caregivers’ own vaccination status was linked to higher vaccine uptake for their children. The study highlights the importance of targeted communication through trusted sources to address vaccine hesitancy. However, it does not provide detailed insights into the mechanisms of hesitancy or specific strategies to improve vaccine acceptance.

title: Co-administration of intranasal parainfluenza virus vaccines expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 S antigens elicits broad and durable immunity in hamsters

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the breadth of immunity and durability of protection elicited by co-administration of two live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3) vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins in hamsters.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in hamsters using two B/HPIV3 vectors expressing the spike protein from the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 isolate (B/HPIV3/S-6P) and the BA.5/Omicron variant (B/HPIV3/S-BA.5-2P). The design involved co-administration of these vectors to assess immune responses and protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed live-attenuated B/HPIV3 vectors with human PIV3 glycoproteins and evaluated their ability to induce anti-S IgG and IgA antibody levels in hamsters. They also assessed neutralizing antibody responses and protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge.
analysis.main_results: Co-administration of the two B/HPIV3 vectors increased the breadth of the S-specific antibody response, spanning the breadth elicited by each vector individually. Hamsters immunized with the mixture developed neutralizing antibodies to both ancestral and recently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains and were protected against BA.5/Omicron challenge 5 months post-immunization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that co-administration of B/HPIV3 vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins can elicit broad and durable immunity, which may offer better protection against emerging variants.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this mucosal immunization approach could provide durable and broad protection against SARS-CoV-2, potentially improving vaccine strategies for combating emerging variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a hamster model, which may not fully represent human immune responses. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates durable protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge with no weight loss or inflammatory responses observed.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immune response and protection elicited by co-administering two live-attenuated bovine/human parainfluenza virus type 3 (B/HPIV3) vectors expressing antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins in hamsters. The vectors were designed to induce broad and durable mucosal and systemic immunity. Results showed that co-administration increased the breadth of the S-specific antibody response and provided long-term protection against BA.5/Omicron challenge, with no weight loss, virus replication, or inflammatory cytokine increase observed. The authors suggest that this approach may offer improved protection against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants. The study is limited to a hamster model, but the evidence supports the durability and breadth of immunity induced by the vaccine strategy.

title: Comparative Burden of COVID-19 in Adults with Rheumatic Diseases and Immunocompetent Individuals: A Population-Based Cohort Study in Quebec, Canada, 2020-2023

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the burden of severe COVID-19 between individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) and immunocompetent individuals, addressing the knowledge gap about the impact of rheumatic diseases on pandemic outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This population-based cohort study analyzed administrative datasets from Quebec, Canada, spanning 2020 to 2023, including 81,434 adults with SARDs, 2,020,356 with comorbidities, and 3,144,700 without comorbidities.
analysis.methods: The study used administrative datasets to estimate crude and age- and sex-standardized incidences of SARS-CoV-2 and severe COVID-19, applying Cox models to derive adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for infection, hospitalization, and ICU/death across different pandemic periods.
analysis.main_results: The SARDS cohort had higher risks of hospitalization and ICU/death compared to immunocompetent individuals during the pre-vaccination period (aHRs: 3.4, 95%CI:2.8–4.1; and 4.0, 95%CI:2.8–5.7, respectively), with these risks persisting through the Omicron period (aHRs: 4.5, 95%CI:4.0–4.9; and 4.4, 95%CI:3.6–5.4, respectively).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that individuals with SARDs, particularly those on highly immunosuppressive therapies, faced elevated risks of severe outcomes, highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the prioritization of SARDS patients in public health measures, emphasizing the importance of tailored surveillance and interventions during future pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on administrative data, which may introduce biases, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the design and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the burden of severe COVID-19 among adults with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) and immunocompetent individuals in Quebec, Canada, from 2020 to 2023. It found that individuals with SARDs had higher risks of hospitalization and ICU/death, particularly during the pre-vaccination and Omicron periods, even after adjusting for age and sex. The results suggest that SARDS patients, especially those on immunosuppressive therapies, require prioritized public health considerations. The study used administrative datasets and Cox models to analyze outcomes, but its observational design and reliance on existing data limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

title: In Silico Investigation of Variant-Specific G-Quadruplex Ligands Targeting the Conserved Main Protease of SARS-CoV-2

analysis.research_question_and_background: The ongoing SARS-CoV-2 pandemic highlights the need for antivirals effective across emerging variants. This study aimed to explore G-quadruplex (G4) ligands as variant-specific inhibitors targeting the conserved main protease (Mpro).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This in silico study analyzed 5.8 million GISAID sequences to identify mutations in the Mpro enzyme. It focused on SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Omicron (JN.1), and selected representative Mpro structures for screening.
analysis.methods: The study used molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations to evaluate ligand interactions with the Mpro enzyme. ADMET predictions were also conducted to assess drug-like properties and potential liabilities.
analysis.main_results: Analysis of GISAID sequences revealed frequent mutations K90R (Alpha), G15S (Lambda), and P132H (Omicron, JN.1). Four ligands, G4L3501, G4L3503, G4L3505, and G4L3506, were identified as stably occupying the catalytic pocket through conserved interactions with His41, Cys145, Glu166, and Gln189.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Per-residue energy decomposition confirmed strong stabilization by active-site residues, consistent with the nirmatrelvir (PF-07321332) binding mode. This suggests that G4 ligands could serve as promising scaffolds for cross-variant Mpro inhibition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the development of G4 ligands as potential antivirals for SARS-CoV-2 and highlight the value of integrating genomic surveillance with molecular modeling to guide drug discovery.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico analysis, and experimental assays are required to confirm inhibitory activity and refine pharmacokinetic properties. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on computational methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated G-quadruplex (G4) ligands as potential antivirals targeting the conserved main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 across emerging variants. By analyzing 5.8 million GISAID sequences, the researchers identified mutations guiding the selection of representative Mpro structures for in silico screening. Molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and MM/GBSA calculations revealed four ligands that stably interact with the catalytic pocket through conserved residues. ADMET predictions indicated moderate drug-likeness but potential issues with intestinal absorption and CYP inhibition. The results suggest that G4 ligands could be promising scaffolds for cross-variant Mpro inhibition, though experimental validation is needed. The study highlights the importance of integrating genomic surveillance with molecular modeling for antiviral development.

title: Rethinking non-human primate models for emerging viral infections after COVID-19

analysis.scope_and_question: Non-human primates (NHPs) retain particular value in emerging viral infection research when questions require integrated analysis of systemic viral kinetics, protective immunity, tissue pathology, or longitudinal outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: However, their cost, limited availability, specialized husbandry, and ethical constraints preclude their routine use as default screening platforms.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Using severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as a case study, we compare how rhesus macaques, cynomolgus macaques, African green monkeys, baboons, and marmosets have contributed to studies of pathogenesis, vaccine protection, therapeutic efficacy, immune memory, and post-acute outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: We emphasize that these species-question relationships cannot be transferred uncritically to future pathogens; model suitability must be re-established according to receptor usage, tissue tropism, disease phenotype, and experimental objective.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: AI-guided prediction, human organoids, and organ-on-chip systems can support this process by prioritizing variants and candidates, identifying tissue-specific mechanisms, and refining endpoints before NHP studies begin.

analysis.summary_en: This review article discusses the role of non-human primate models in emerging viral infection research, with a focus on SARS-CoV-2. It highlights the value of NHPs in studying systemic viral kinetics, protective immunity, tissue pathology, and longitudinal outcomes. However, the article also notes the limitations of NHPs, including cost, availability, specialized care, and ethical concerns, which prevent their routine use. The study compares the contributions of various primate species to understanding SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis, vaccine protection, therapeutic efficacy, immune memory, and post-acute outcomes. It stresses that the suitability of these models for future pathogens must be re-evaluated based on specific factors like receptor usage, tissue tropism, and disease phenotype. The article proposes integrating computational and human-relevant platforms to narrow evidence gaps before using NHPs, which can enhance interpretability, reproducibility, and alignment with the 3Rs while preserving their use for complex biological questions.

title: COVID-19, immunity, and vaccination: unravelling the interplay of sex, gender, age, and the exposome

analysis.scope_and_question: Sex- and gender-related differences profoundly influence immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination but remain insufficiently considered in research and public health strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review explores how sex, gender, age, and the exposome interact to shape susceptibility to coronavirus-19 disease (COVID-19), disease severity, Long COVID, and vaccine-induced immunity.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Males experience higher rates of severe disease, hospitalisation, and mortality, whereas females generally mount stronger innate and adaptive immune responses, contributing to greater resilience. Current evidence on Long COVID is discussed, including its higher prevalence among females and the sex-specific immunological pathways that may underlie persistent symptoms. We examine age-, sex-, and gender-related differences in vaccine response, distinguishing efficacy from effectiveness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: These differences arise from a complex interplay between biological factors and gender-related determinants, including occupational exposures, healthcare access, health-related behaviours, socioeconomic conditions, and the microbiota, which contribute to the individual exposome. The relative benefit of vaccination appears greater in males because of their higher baseline risk of severe disease. Although females generally mount stronger antibody responses, this advantage does not necessarily translate into greater clinical protection.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrating sex, gender, age, and the exposome perspectives is essential for developing more equitable and personalised strategies to prevent and manage COVID-19 and future emerging diseases. Finally, we discuss how exposomic factors, including lifestyle, microbiota composition, and environmental and social determinants, influence vaccine responsiveness and hesitancy.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines how sex, gender, age, and the exposome interact to influence susceptibility, disease severity, Long COVID, and vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2. It highlights that males are at higher risk of severe disease, hospitalisation, and mortality, while females tend to have stronger immune responses. The review also discusses the role of exposomic factors, such as lifestyle, microbiota, and social determinants, in shaping vaccine responses and hesitancy. Despite stronger antibody responses in females, this does not always equate to greater clinical protection. The findings underscore the need to integrate sex, gender, and exposome perspectives into public health strategies to create more equitable and personalized approaches for managing SARS-CoV-2 and future diseases.

title: Serious cardiac events in the COVID-19 era in the paediatric population: what did we learn?

analysis.scope_and_question: Serious cardiac events, which are frequently associated with myocarditis or arrhythmias, pose serious public health concerns. This narrative review compares serious cardiac event incidence, mechanisms, and outcomes in adults and children.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Data were gathered from peer-reviewed studies between 2019 and 2025, such as systematic reviews, clinical reports, and cohort analyses. Focus was placed on the potential contribution of COVID-19-related cardiac events.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: While vaccine-related cardiac complications are still uncommon, COVID-19 infection is linked to an increased risk of serious cardiac events in adults. Paediatric serious cardiac events, on the other hand, are rare but frequently associated with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children, and there have been rare, documented vaccine-associated deaths in this population. Significant findings reveal clear patterns in serious cardiac events mechanisms, with age-dependent differences in the severity and prognosis of COVID-19-related myocarditis, arrhythmias, and long QT syndrome, among others.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Important knowledge gaps about the long-term cardiac effects of COVID-19 still exist. These lead to the possibility of unusual or delayed cardiac consequences and the requirement for specialised monitoring techniques to reduce potential risks, particularly in high-risk populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Key research and clinical practice gaps were identified by analysing paediatric and adult populations in terms of diagnostic methods, management techniques, and long-term results. These variations highlight the necessity of age-appropriate risk assessment and management techniques. In the context of COVID-19, these findings highlight distinct risk profiles for serious cardiac events, underscoring the need for targeted screening methods and focused public health initiatives.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores serious cardiac events in the pediatric population during the COVID-19 era, focusing on their association with myocarditis, arrhythmias, and multisystem inflammatory syndrome. It highlights the increased risk of such events in adults linked to COVID-19 infection, while noting that pediatric cases are rare but often tied to multisystem inflammatory syndrome. Vaccine-related cardiac complications are uncommon, though rare vaccine-associated deaths have been documented. The review identifies age-dependent differences in the mechanisms and prognosis of these events, emphasizing the need for tailored risk assessments and monitoring strategies. Despite some consensus, significant knowledge gaps remain, particularly regarding long-term cardiac effects and the necessity for specialized diagnostic and management approaches in high-risk groups.

title: SARS-CoV-2 severity and vaccination, pneumonia, and the risk of Stroke: A nationwide, nested case-control study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Infections, including SARS-CoV-2, may increase stroke risk, but the roles of COVID-19 severity, vaccination, and comparison with other respiratory infections remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study examined the association between COVID-19, its severity, and vaccination status with the incidence of new-onset total stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and ischemic stroke in a nationwide sample of adults aged ≥50 years.
analysis.methods: A nested case-control study was conducted within the largest healthcare provider in Israel. Stroke-free individuals were followed-up from March 2020 to May 2022. Incident total, ICH and ischemic stroke cases were matched 1:10 to controls by age, sex, and index date.
analysis.main_results: Among 1,198,088 eligible participants, 11,974 individuals with incident total stroke were matched to 119,740 controls. COVID-19 was associated with an increased stroke risk (OR=1.23; 95% CI 1.16-1.30; P < 0.001). Vaccination was associated with lower stroke risk, although this observational association warrants cautious interpretation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that COVID-19 requiring hospitalization confers an acute, time-limited increase in stroke risk, of a magnitude somewhat lower than that observed after pneumonia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted cerebrovascular surveillance following hospitalization for respiratory infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and thus the association between vaccination and lower stroke risk warrants cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection, its severity, and vaccination status with the risk of stroke in adults aged ≥50 years. Conducted as a nationwide nested case-control study within Israel's largest healthcare provider, the research followed stroke-free individuals from March 2020 to May 2022. It found that COVID-19 was linked to an increased stroke risk (OR=1.23; 95% CI 1.16-1.30; P < 0.001), while vaccination was associated with lower risk. The authors suggest that cerebrovascular surveillance should be targeted following hospitalization for respiratory infections. However, the observational nature of the study means the link between vaccination and reduced stroke risk requires careful interpretation. The study provides insights into the acute stroke risk associated with SARS-CoV-2 hospitalization, though it does not establish causality.

title: Emerging Biomarkers Across the Clinical Spectrum of SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Long COVID

analysis.scope_and_question: For consistency, this review uses the term “Long COVID” throughout; PASC and PACS are noted only where they reflect the terminology used by a specific cited study.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on candidate biomarkers relevant to SARS-CoV-2 infection, with particular attention to their mechanistic, clinical and translational relevance to long COVID specifically.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Reflecting the fact that many candidate markers have been characterised primarily in acute or severe COVID-19, we explicitly indicate, for each biomarker domain, the strength and directness of the evidence linking it to long COVID as opposed to acute disease severity alone, and we distinguish exploratory candidates from those with more established clinical utility.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Relative to prior systematic reviews of long COVID biomarkers, this review’s distinguishing contribution is its explicit separation of acute-phase from chronic-phase evidence, its integration of genetic, epigenetic, and multiomics data within a single mechanistic framework, and its tiered classification of biomarkers by clinical readiness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The absence of validated, clinically actionable biomarkers remains a major barrier to diagnosis, risk stratification, and targeted intervention.

analysis.summary_en: For consistency, this review uses the term “Long COVID” throughout; PASC and PACS are noted only where they reflect the terminology used by a specific cited study. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on candidate biomarkers relevant to SARS-CoV-2 infection, with particular attention to their mechanistic, clinical and translational relevance to long COVID specifically. Reflecting the fact that many candidate markers have been characterised primarily in acute or severe COVID-19, we explicitly indicate, for each biomarker domain, the strength and directness of the evidence linking it to long COVID as opposed to acute disease severity alone, and we distinguish exploratory candidates from those with more established clinical utility. Relative to prior systematic reviews of long COVID biomarkers, this review’s distinguishing contribution is its explicit separation of acute-phase from chronic-phase evidence, its integration of genetic, epigenetic, and multiomics data within a single mechanistic framework, and its tiered classification of biomarkers by clinical readiness. The absence of validated, clinically actionable biomarkers remains a major barrier to diagnosis, risk stratification, and targeted intervention.

title: Immunogenicity and vaccine effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines in people on immunosuppressive therapies

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between neutralizing antibodies and protection against SARS-CoV-2 in people on immunosuppressive therapies, as data on correlates of protection often exclude these individuals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A systematic search was conducted to identify studies on SARS-CoV-2 binding antibody levels after mRNA vaccination in people with hematological malignancies, neurological disorders, rheumatic diseases, and mixed immune-mediated inflammatory disorders on immunosuppressive therapies, as well as healthy controls.
analysis.methods: The study used data from a previous analysis of vaccine effectiveness in people with the same underlying conditions and linked these estimates with predicted antibody levels derived from a meta-analysis of binding antibody levels.
analysis.main_results: Binding antibody levels varied across cohorts receiving different immunosuppressive treatments, with the lowest levels observed in those treated with B-cell depletion and S1P inhibitors. Predicted neutralizing antibody levels were correlated with vaccine effectiveness for both infection and hospitalization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that antibody levels are associated with vaccine effectiveness, but emphasized that immunosuppressed individuals have lower protection at any given antibody level compared to healthy populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform strategies for monitoring vaccine responses in immunosuppressed individuals and guide the development of more effective vaccination protocols for this vulnerable group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on data from a previous analysis and predicted antibody levels, which may introduce limitations in the accuracy of the correlation between antibody levels and protection, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between neutralizing antibodies and protection against SARS-CoV-2 in people on immunosuppressive therapies, as existing data often excludes these individuals. A systematic search identified antibody levels after mRNA vaccination in various immune conditions, revealing significant reductions in B-cell depletion and S1P inhibitor treatments. The authors linked these antibody levels with vaccine effectiveness data from a prior study, finding a correlation between antibody levels and protection against infection and hospitalization. However, they noted that immunosuppressed individuals have lower protection at any given antibody level compared to healthy controls. These results may inform strategies for monitoring vaccine responses in immunosuppressed populations. The study's reliance on predicted antibody levels and prior data limits its evidence strength, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Immune dysfunction in chronic lymphocytic leukemia : translational and epidemiological studies during the COVID-19 pandemic

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination on individuals with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) during the COVID-19 pandemic, given the known immune deficiencies in CLL patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study included five distinct investigations. Study I examined CLL patients in the Stockholm region during the early pandemic, Study II compared CLL patients with healthy controls in the COVAXID trial, Study III focused on hybrid immunity in recovered patients, Study IV analyzed vaccine uptake in Sweden using national registries, and Study V evaluated mortality and hospitalization rates across the first three years of the pandemic.
analysis.methods: Study I collected clinical data from medical records and followed patients with repeated blood and saliva samples for up to 12 months. Study II used data from the COVAXID trial, including blood and saliva samples before and after vaccination. Study IV utilized six national health and sociodemographic registries to track vaccination uptake over time.
analysis.main_results: In Study I, 77% of CLL patients required hospitalization, 24% needed intensive care, and approximately 30% died. In Study II, 60% of CLL patients seroconverted with low antibody titers, while T cell responses were observed in 29% of patients. In Study IV, 94% of CLL patients received two doses, 88% three doses, 78% four doses, and 56% five doses of the vaccine. In Study V, the adjusted risk ratio for 90-day all-cause mortality was 1.70 in CLL patients compared to comparators, with higher risks among younger patients and those on certain treatments.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that CLL patients experience more severe outcomes from SARS-CoV-2 infection, but vaccine doses appear to reduce the risk of poor outcomes. The study also highlights disparities in vaccine uptake among different demographic groups within the CLL population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform strategies for vaccination and infection prevention in CLL patients, emphasizing the need for tailored approaches and addressing disparities in vaccine access and uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on registry data and medical records, which may introduce bias or missing information. However, the evidence is robust due to the use of multiple national datasets and longitudinal tracking of vaccine uptake.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination on individuals with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) during the COVID-19 pandemic. It includes five investigations: Study I assessed clinical and immunological outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection in CLL patients, revealing high hospitalization and mortality rates. Study II evaluated vaccine responses in CLL patients and healthy controls, showing lower seroconversion and T cell responses in CLL patients. Study IV analyzed vaccine uptake in Sweden, finding higher rates among CLL patients than the general population but significant disparities by age, region of birth, and income. Study V compared mortality and hospitalization rates between CLL patients and the general population, noting increased risks for younger patients and those on certain treatments. The findings suggest that while CLL patients face heightened risks from SARS-CoV-2, vaccination reduces these risks. The study highlights the importance of targeted vaccination strategies and addressing disparities in vaccine access for this vulnerable group.

title: Increased In-Hospital Mortality in Immunocompromised Individuals Hospitalized With COVID-19 During the Global Pandemic: A Multinational Cohort Study in the EuCARE Project.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether immunocompromising conditions (ICCs) still pose an increased mortality risk during the Omicron era of the COVID-19 pandemic. Although coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is no longer a public health emergency, it remains the most prevalent circulating infectious-like illness in Europe.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multinational cohort study was conducted across EuCARE sites in 8 countries among adults hospitalized with COVID-19 between 2020 and 2023. A total of 42,488 individuals were included, of whom 1,675 (3.9%) had an ICC.
analysis.methods: ICCs and COVID-19 pneumonia at hospitalization were defined using clinical information and ICD-10 codes. Logistic regression and counterfactual mediation analysis were used to compare 28-day in-hospital mortality risk associated with ICCs, using COVID-19 pneumonia and vaccination at hospital entry as intermediates. Proportion of the total effect of ICCs mediated and the controlled direct effects (CDEs) were calculated. The study also formally tested for interaction between SARS-CoV-2 variants and ICCs for mortality risk.
analysis.main_results: ICCs were associated with increased mortality (OR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.25-1.79]). There was no evidence for an attenuation during the Omicron phase (P value for interaction = .60). Mediation analyses showed that the total effect of ICCs was mediated by vaccination but only weakly by pneumonia. With Omicron, the excess mortality associated with ICC was higher under the scenario that everyone in the cohort was to develop COVID-19 pneumonia (CDE, 1.22 [95% CI, .09-1.65]).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that ICC remains a significant risk factor for in-hospital death, even during the Omicron era, particularly if the infection led to the development of pneumonia. This finding highlights the persistent impact of immunocompromising conditions on mortality outcomes despite the emergence of the Omicron variant.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that immunocompromised individuals hospitalized with COVID-19 continue to face heightened mortality risks, even with the Omicron variant. This has important implications for targeted surveillance, diagnosis, and management strategies for immunocompromised patients during future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on clinical information and ICD-10 codes for defining ICCs and pneumonia, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate, as the study is based on an abstract-only analysis and does not provide detailed statistical or methodological information.

analysis.summary_en: This multinational cohort study investigated whether immunocompromising conditions (ICCs) still increase in-hospital mortality risk during the Omicron era of the COVID-19 pandemic. The study included 42,488 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 between 2020 and 2023, of whom 3.9% had ICCs. Results showed that ICCs were associated with increased mortality (OR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.25-1.79]) with no evidence of attenuation during the Omicron phase. Mediation analyses indicated that vaccination played a more significant role in mediating the effect of ICCs on mortality than pneumonia. The authors concluded that ICC remains a significant risk factor for in-hospital death, particularly when pneumonia develops. The study's findings have implications for public health strategies targeting immunocompromised individuals, but the evidence is moderate due to reliance on abstract-only data and potential biases in defining ICCs and pneumonia.

title: Self-Rated Health and Persistent Symptoms Among Adults Reporting Previous SARS-CoV-2 Infection: A Cross-Sectional Study

analysis.scope_and_question: This study investigated the relationship between self-rated health and persistent symptoms among adults who had previously experienced SARS-CoV-2 infection. The central question was whether current health ratings differ from those recalled before infection and what sociodemographic and clinical factors are associated with these ratings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional survey of 120 adults was conducted at University Clinical Hospital No. 4 in Lublin, Poland, and online between January and April 2026. The study used an author-designed questionnaire to assess sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, current and recalled pre-infection general health, and symptoms following coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Bivariate analyses were performed using non-parametric tests and chi-square tests, with p < 0.05 as the nominal significance threshold.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Current health ratings were less favorable than recalled pre-infection health in this sample. The most commonly reported current complaints were fatigue/weakness, cognitive disturbances (‘brain fog’), and dyspnoea. Current health ratings were associated with age, education, employment, financial situation, and reported disease severity. Mean normalised GHQ-30 domain scores indicated moderate psychological symptoms, with poorer financial situation and more hospitalisations showing small positive correlations with poorer GHQ-30 scores. Vaccine dose count showed a small correlation with general functioning.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study acknowledges limitations such as recall bias, selection effects, and unmeasured or uncontrolled confounding, which prevent definitive attribution of the observed health differences to SARS-CoV-2 infection. The exploratory associations do not establish independent risk factors, clinical diagnoses, or population prevalence. The study does not address the long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection or provide data on specific variants.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to explore the long-term health impacts of SARS-CoV-2 infection, including the effects of specific variants. Surveillance and diagnostic efforts should focus on identifying persistent symptoms and their correlates. Public health policies should consider the socioeconomic factors influencing health outcomes in post-infection populations.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study examined self-rated health and persistent symptoms among 120 adults with a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection. It found that current health ratings were less favorable than those recalled before infection, with fatigue, cognitive disturbances, and dyspnoea being the most common complaints. Factors such as age, education, employment, financial situation, and disease severity were associated with current health ratings. Psychological symptoms were measured using the GHQ-30, with moderate scores indicating anxiety and depression. The study highlights the need for further research on long-term effects, persistent symptoms, and socioeconomic influences on health outcomes post-infection.

title: Indole-based peptidomimetic maleimides as SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitor scaffolds compatible with reversible covalent inhibition: Warhead optimization and broad in vitro antiviral activity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed due to the continued evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and the emergence of resistance-associated mutations, which highlight the need for additional inhibitor scaffolds with balanced potency, chemical stability, and reversible covalent reactivity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports the discovery and warhead optimization of indole-based peptidomimetic maleimides as Mpro inhibitor scaffolds with a binding mode compatible with reversible covalent inhibition.
analysis.methods: Initial attempts to access α-cyanoacrylate analogues resulted in product-related fractions whose chromatographic and mass-spectrometric profiles changed during purification and analytical handling, preventing isolation of analytically pure samples for biological profiling.
analysis.main_results: DFT calculations showed higher electrophilicity for the α-cyanoacrylate model and provided a supportive electronic rationale for the contrasting purification and handling behavior of the two warhead classes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Subsequent optimization of the maleimide series identified compound 8i as the lead inhibitor, with single-digit nanomolar inhibition of wild-type Mpro (IC50 = 6.51 nM).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: In P-gp inhibitor-supplemented Vero E6 CPE assays, 8i showed broad in vitro antiviral activity against wild-type, Delta, and Omicron BA.5 SARS-CoV-2 variants, with EC50 values of 1.44, 0.49, and 1.52 μM, respectively, while 50% cytotoxicity was not reached at concentrations up to 100 μM under the applied assay conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Because biochemical activity against the selected mutant proteases has not been experimentally determined, the docking results should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating structural models rather than evidence of mutation tolerance.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the need for additional SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) inhibitors due to the virus's continued evolution and emergence of resistance-associated mutations. The researchers focused on developing indole-based peptidomimetic maleimides as potential Mpro inhibitor scaffolds with reversible covalent inhibition properties. Initial attempts to synthesize α-cyanoacrylate analogues led to impure samples, complicating biological profiling. DFT calculations provided insights into the electrophilicity differences between the two warhead classes. Optimization of the maleimide series identified compound 8i as a lead inhibitor with single-digit nanomolar potency against wild-type Mpro. In vitro antiviral activity of 8i was demonstrated against wild-type, Delta, and Omicron BA.5 variants, with EC50 values of 1.44, 0.49, and 1.52 μM, respectively, and no observed cytotoxicity up to 100 μM. Covalent docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported the structural interpretation of the modeled Mpro complexes. However, the docking results were noted as hypothesis-generating models rather than evidence of mutation tolerance. These findings suggest that indole-based peptidomimetic maleimides could serve as chemically tractable scaffolds for further antiviral optimization.

title: Changes in Dengue Epidemiology in China Before, During, and After COVID-19 2015-2024: A Retrospective National Surveillance and Spatiotemporal Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains a major mosquito-borne disease in China. However, comprehensive nationwide evidence on their long-term epidemiological impact is limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a nationwide retrospective spatiotemporal study using reported dengue cases in China from 2015 to 2024. Epidemiological characteristics were compared across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic phases.
analysis.methods: Morlet wavelet analysis was used to assess temporal periodicity. A SARIMA model fitted to pre-pandemic data generated counterfactual forecasts for 2020-2024. Spatial patterns were evaluated using provincial incidence mapping, Global Moran's I, and Local Indicators of Spatial Association.
analysis.main_results: A total of 87 182 dengue cases were reported, with major peaks in 2019 and 2024. Importing cases declined sharply during 2020-2022 and rebounded after 2023, whereas indigenous transmission became increasingly dominant. Annual periodicity weakened during the pandemic but re-emerged after 2023. Observed incidence during 2020-2022 was frequently below counterfactual expectations, while substantial positive deviations appeared from mid-2023 and intensified in 2024. Post-pandemic dengue risk re-emerged in South and Southwest China and expanded inland, with weaker provincial clustering.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: COVID-19 and related NPIs substantially reshaped dengue epidemiology in China, suppressing transmission during 2020-2022 but followed by a marked post-pandemic resurgence, increasing indigenous transmission, disrupted but re-emerging seasonality, and broader inland spread.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can cautiously inform surveillance strategies, risk assessment, and public health interventions for dengue in China, particularly in understanding the interplay between pandemic-related measures and dengue transmission dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on reported dengue cases and does not account for unreported or underdiagnosed cases. The evidence is moderate as it relies on retrospective analysis and statistical modeling.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines changes in dengue epidemiology in China from 2015 to 2024, focusing on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and associated interventions. It highlights a decline in imported dengue cases during the pandemic, a shift toward indigenous transmission, and a post-pandemic resurgence with broader inland spread. The research uses spatiotemporal analysis, Morlet wavelet analysis, and SARIMA modeling to assess these changes. The findings suggest that pandemic-related measures significantly altered dengue transmission dynamics, with implications for public health surveillance and intervention strategies. However, the study's reliance on reported data and statistical modeling limits the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

title: Shared Clinical and Immunological Features of Post-Acute COVID-19 and Post-Acute COVID-19 Vaccination Syndromes

analysis.research_question_and_background: Post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) can cause persistent disability involving fatigue, post-exertional malaise, neurocognitive symptoms, and autonomic manifestations. A clinically overlapping condition has been reported following COVID-19 vaccination and termed post-acute COVID-19 vaccination syndrome (PACVS), but its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study included 28 PACS patients, 29 PACVS patients, and 16 convalescent controls (CCG).
analysis.methods: Clinical manifestations were assessed using ME/CFS-related symptom questionnaires and the Bell Score. T-cell phenotypes and T cells reactive to SARS-CoV-2 Spike, {beta}1/{beta}2-adrenergic receptor, and M3/M4 muscarinic receptor antigens were analyzed by multicolor flow cytometry. Circulating Spike protein and GPCR autoantibodies were quantified by ELISA, and EBV load by qPCR.
analysis.main_results: PACS and PACVS showed substantial clinical overlap, although several symptoms were more severe in PACS. GPCR autoantibody profiles were comparable between patient groups, while {beta}2-adrenergic receptor autoantibodies were increased compared with CCG. Only three of 57 conventional immunophenotyping parameters differed between PACS and PACVS in unadjusted analyses, whereas both groups showed multiple alterations compared with CCG. Circulating Spike protein was detected in both patient groups, with the highest prevalence in PACVS. {beta}1/{beta}2- and M3/M4-reactive CD4+ T cells were increased, whereas Spike-specific CD4+ T cells were reduced compared with CCG. EBV reactivation was rare.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: PACS and PACVS exhibit substantial clinical and immunological overlap, including GPCR-directed autoreactivity and altered receptor-reactive T-cell responses. These shared immune-mediated features suggest overlapping pathophysiological mechanisms and warrant investigation of whether therapeutic strategies currently explored for PACS may also be relevant to PACVS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that immune-mediated mechanisms may underlie both PACS and PACVS, which could inform the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for these conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size, but the evidence is strong as it directly compares immunological features between PACS and PACVS patients.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the clinical and immunological features of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) and post-acute COVID-19 vaccination syndrome (PACVS). It reports substantial clinical overlap between the two conditions, with PACS showing more severe symptoms. Immunological analyses reveal shared features such as GPCR-directed autoreactivity and altered T-cell responses, suggesting overlapping pathophysiological mechanisms. The study highlights the potential relevance of therapeutic strategies for PACS to PACVS. However, the cross-sectional design and small sample size limit the confidence in the findings, though the evidence is strong due to direct comparisons of immunological profiles.

title: Towards an understanding of COVID-19-associated preeclampsia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy has been associated with higher rates of preeclampsia (PE). The study aimed to explore the molecular mechanisms underlying this association.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted bulk RNA sequencing on placental tissues from four pregnancy groups: uneventful prepandemic (preCOVID-19), prepandemic PE (preCOVID-19 PE), COVID-19 without PE (COVID no PE), and COVID-19 complicated by PE or other hypertensive disorders (COVID PE).
analysis.methods: Differential expression was analyzed using Deseq2 likelihood ratio test (LRT), and gene set enrichment analysis identified dysregulated pathways.
analysis.main_results: Clustering of LRT-significant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) identified a set of 16 genes (defined by the false discovery rate adjusted p-value < 0.05) across the four pregnancy groups, showing stepwise expression changes-lowest in preCOVID-19 uneventful, followed by those in COVID-19 without PE, then preCOVID-19 PE, and highest in COVID PE.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings identify a COVID-19-associated placental signature that mirrors PE features and shows a progressive expression pattern defining a continuum of placental stress, with maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection potentially exacerbating underlying dysfunction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms linking SARS-CoV-2 infection to preeclampsia, which could inform future research on placental stress and guide targeted interventions for pregnant individuals with COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to placental tissue analysis and does not account for other potential confounding factors. The evidence is moderate as it is based on RNA sequencing and gene set enrichment analysis without direct clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms linking SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy to preeclampsia. By analyzing placental tissues from four groups—uneventful prepandemic, prepandemic PE, COVID-19 without PE, and COVID-19 complicated by PE—the researchers identified a set of 16 differentially expressed genes showing a stepwise expression pattern. These genes were associated with placental dysfunction, and immune activation pathways were predominantly enriched in the COVID PE group. The findings suggest a potential continuum of placental stress, with maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection possibly exacerbating underlying dysfunction. The study provides moderate evidence for understanding the molecular basis of this association, though it does not account for other confounding factors.

title: Cysteine supplementation reverses immune dysfunction in cancer patients with severe COVID-19

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the immunologic dysfunction in cancer patients with severe COVID-19 and to identify a therapeutic strategy to address this dysfunction. Severe COVID-19 in cancer patients is characterized by muted adaptive immune responses, and the molecular drivers of this dysfunction remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved cancer and non-cancer patients with or without COVID-19, comparing proteomic and metabolomic profiles to identify dysfunctional cysteine metabolism associated with severe COVID-19 in cancer patients.
analysis.methods: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed on matched cohorts of cancer and non-cancer patients with or without COVID-19 to identify dysfunctional cysteine metabolism.
analysis.main_results: N-acetylcysteine (N-AC) treatment improved clinical outcomes in cancer patients with steroid-refractory COVID-19, reducing markers of innate inflammation, decreasing severe disease-associated MHC-II low monocytes, and increasing circulating CD8+ T cell abundance, activation, and effector differentiation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: N-AC treatment mechanistically reduced prostaglandin E2-driven interactions between suppressive monocytes and T cells, enabling clonal expansion and effector T cell differentiation, and enhanced lung-infiltrating CD8+ T cell abundance in murine models.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Cysteine supplementation with N-AC can therapeutically reverse redox-driven immune dysregulation in severe respiratory viral infection, particularly in the high-risk cancer population, establishing it as a viable therapeutic strategy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a prospective clinical trial and murine models, and the generalizability of the findings to other patient populations is uncertain.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified dysfunctional cysteine metabolism in cancer patients with severe COVID-19 and demonstrated that N-acetylcysteine (N-AC) treatment improves clinical outcomes and immune function, suggesting cysteine supplementation as a therapeutic strategy.

title: Association between the glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio and prognosis in COVID-19 patients

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the associations between GLR and disease severity as well as clinical outcomes among hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has transitioned into an endemic stage and is no longer classified as a public health emergency of international concern.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort enrolled 235 hospitalized COVID-19 patients infected during the Omicron BA.5 and BF.7 wave from December 29, 2022 to January 15, 2023. All patients were followed up until the unified cutoff date of February 18, 2023, with all-cause mortality set as the primary endpoint.
analysis.methods: We measured inflammatory markers, the metabolic marker, and T-cell immune parameters to validate our a priori hypothesis that glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio (GLR) mirrors concurrent inflammation. We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 235 individuals with COVID-19 to explore the prognostic value of GLR levels at diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: Our findings revealed that GLR levels were significantly higher in severe patients than in mild-to-moderate patients. Meanwhile, beta2-microglobulin (β2-MG), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and interleukin-10 (IL-10) were significantly elevated in the high GLR group, whereas apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), CD3 absolute value, CD4 absolute value, and CD8 absolute value were significantly lower.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our data confirmed that GLR levels at initial diagnosis were significantly correlated with disease severity and prognosis in patients with COVID-19. According to multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, GLR ( P = 0.003) was found to be an independent, adverse prognostic factor for OS in Omicron patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: As an easily calculated metabolic-immune indicator, GLR acts as a promising complementary candidate biomarker for mortality risk stratification in Omicron COVID-19 patients. Further independent external validation is required before its routine clinical application.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The two groups only partially overlapped, so high GLR is not equivalent to severe illness. The supplied evidence does not report the specific statistical methods used to assess the association between GLR and clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between the glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio (GLR) and prognosis in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during the Omicron BA.5 and BF.7 wave. The research aimed to explore how GLR levels correlate with disease severity and clinical outcomes. A retrospective cohort of 235 patients was analyzed, with follow-up until February 18, 2023, using all-cause mortality as the primary endpoint. The study measured inflammatory markers, metabolic indicators, and T-cell immune parameters to validate the hypothesis that GLR reflects concurrent inflammation. Results showed that GLR levels were significantly higher in severe patients compared to mild-to-moderate ones, and several other biomarkers were also associated with high GLR. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analysis confirmed that GLR was an independent adverse prognostic factor for overall survival. The authors concluded that GLR could serve as a promising biomarker for mortality risk stratification in Omicron patients, though further validation is needed for clinical use. The study's limitations include partial overlap between groups, suggesting high GLR is not synonymous with severe illness.

title: The Multidimensional Impact of COVID-19 and Post-COVID-19 Conditions on Sexual and Reproductive Health: A Systematic Review

analysis.scope_and_question: Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The final synthesis included 218 eligible reports, corresponding to 214 conservative study/cohort units after confirmed companion/derived-publication linkage.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Erectile dysfunction was the most consistent sexual outcome, whereas reproductive studies mainly reported reduced semen quality and alterations in testosterone and gonadal-axis markers, often appearing short-term.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: However, the evidence was predominantly male-focused, observational, and heterogeneous, limiting causal and long-term inference.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: COVID-19 may affect sexual and reproductive health through interacting biological and psychosocial pathways, but persistent infertility or definitive reproductive impairment remains unconfirmed.

analysis.summary_en: Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively. The final synthesis included 218 eligible reports, corresponding to 214 conservative study/cohort units after confirmed companion/derived-publication linkage. Erectile dysfunction was the most consistent sexual outcome, whereas reproductive studies mainly reported reduced semen quality and alterations in testosterone and gonadal-axis markers, often appearing short-term. However, the evidence was predominantly male-focused, observational, and heterogeneous, limiting causal and long-term inference. COVID-19 may affect sexual and reproductive health through interacting biological and psychosocial pathways, but persistent infertility or definitive reproductive impairment remains unconfirmed.

title: Para-Aortic Adipose Tissue as Predictor of Severe Acute SARS-CoV-2 Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for severe COVID-19, largely mediated by chronic inflammation originating from adipose tissue. The role of para-aortic adipose tissue (PAT)—a component of perivascular adipose tissue in COVID-19 severity remains poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 279 hospitalized patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia. Based on disease severity, patients were divided into moderate and severe groups.
analysis.methods: PAT volume was measured around the aorta semi-automatically on a single chest computed tomography. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were analyzed. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed to assess the predictive value of PAT volume.
analysis.main_results: Patients with severe COVID-19 were significantly older, had higher body mass index. PAT volume differed significantly between groups, with a greater proportion of higher values in the severe group. Severe cases also exhibited significantly elevated levels of C-reactive protein, ferritin, and D-dimer, and lower oxygen saturation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Correlation analysis revealed significant associations between PAT volume and age, BMI, ferritin, the extent of lung involvement and SpO2. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that log-transformed PAT volume was independently associated with severe COVID-19.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: PAT volume is independently associated with severe COVID-19, and values exceeding 0.35 cm3 may serve as a predictor of disease severity in hospitalized patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between para-aortic adipose tissue (PAT) volume and the severity of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. It aims to evaluate PAT as a predictor of severe COVID-19. The research is based on a retrospective single-center cohort study involving 279 hospitalized patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia, divided into moderate and severe groups. PAT volume was measured semi-automatically on chest computed tomography, and clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were analyzed using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. The results showed that patients with severe COVID-19 were significantly older and had higher BMI. PAT volume was significantly higher in the severe group, and severe cases exhibited elevated levels of C-reactive protein, ferritin, and D-dimer, along with lower oxygen saturation. Correlation analysis found significant associations between PAT volume and age, BMI, ferritin, lung involvement, and SpO2. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that log-transformed PAT volume was independently associated with severe COVID-19. The optimal threshold for initial PAT volume was 0.35 cm3, with sensitivity of 51.2% and specificity of 67.1%. The authors conclude that PAT volume may serve as a predictor of disease severity in hospitalized patients. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's design and the absence of reported limitations.

title: Repurposing Thiazole/Benzothiazole-Based Thiazolidinone Derivatives as SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease (Mpro) Inhibitors: An Integrated Computational and Experimental Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2, the causative agent of COVID-19, relies on its main protease (Mpro) for viral replication, making this enzyme an attractive target for antiviral drug development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In the present study, we investigated whether a library of previously synthesized thiazole/benzothiazole-based thiazolidinone derivatives, originally developed as anti-HIV agents, could be repurposed as SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors.
analysis.methods: A total of 85 thiazole/benzothiazole-based thiazolidinone derivatives were computationally screened against SARS-CoV-2 Mpro using molecular docking. Based on their predicted binding affinities, fifteen were selected for experimental evaluation. Enzymatic assays were used to quantify Mpro inhibition, and the compounds with the clearest enzymatic activity were then examined for their ability to limit viral replication in cell culture models challenged with the Delta and Omicron variants.
analysis.main_results: Molecular docking identified several derivatives with favorable predicted interactions within the Mpro active site. Experimental evaluation revealed five compounds with measurable inhibitory activity against Mpro, exhibiting IC50 values spanning 0.19 to 13.15 μM. Further antiviral testing demonstrated that some of the active compounds reduced viral replication in cell-based assays against both Delta and Omicron variants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrate that thiazole/benzothiazole-based thiazolidinone derivatives represent a promising chemical scaffold for SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitor development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of new antiviral therapies targeting SARS-CoV-2 Mpro, potentially offering alternative treatments for COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A direct correlation between enzymatic inhibition and antiviral efficacy was not observed, indicating that additional pharmacological and cellular factors may influence antiviral activity.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of thiazole/benzothiazole-based thiazolidinone derivatives, originally developed as anti-HIV agents, to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro). Computational screening identified 85 derivatives, with 15 selected for experimental evaluation. Enzymatic assays revealed five compounds with measurable Mpro inhibition, and further testing showed some compounds reduced viral replication in cell culture models against Delta and Omicron variants. The results suggest these derivatives could serve as a promising scaffold for Mpro inhibitor development, though the lack of direct correlation between enzymatic activity and antiviral efficacy highlights the need for further studies. The findings may contribute to the development of new antiviral therapies for COVID-19.
